sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: National and International **Awards & Winners** (पुरस्कार एवं विजेता) covering civilian, bravery, sports, literature, and science categories.
Established across different eras starting from **1901** (Nobel Prize) to **1954** (Bharat Ratna, Padma Awards) and modern annual cycles.
Presented globally (Stockholm, Oslo, New York) and nationally at **Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi** by the President of India.
Awarded to extraordinary individuals and organizations for exceptional contributions in science, arts, literature, public service, and sports.
Crucial static General Awareness section for **UPSSSC PET** carrying **2-3 direct questions** in the exam paper.
Includes highest civilian awards (**Bharat Ratna**), highest sports honors (**Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**), and international accolades (**Nobel, Booker, Pulitzer**).
Tests factual retention of first recipients, latest winners, award money, and sponsoring bodies.
Maximum **3 Bharat Ratna** awards can be given per year; **Padma Awards** are announced annually on **Republic Day** eve.

items.title: 1. India's Highest Civilian Honor: Bharat Ratna
items.content:
• Established in **1954** by President **Rajendra Prasad**.
• Designed in the shape of a **peepal leaf** with a bronze sunburst and platinum inscription.
• **No monetary grant** is given, only a sanad (certificate) and a medallion.
• First recipients (**1954**): **C. Rajagopalachari**, **S. Radhakrishnan**, and **C.V. Raman**.
• First sportsperson and youngest recipient: **Sachin Tendulkar** (**2014**).
• **Mnemonic for First 3:** **"RCR"** -> **R**ajagopalachari, **C**.V. Raman, **R**adhakrishnan.

items.title: 2. Padma Awards Hierarchy & Details
items.content:
• Instituted in **1954**, suspended briefly between **1977-1980** and **1993-1997**.
• **Padma Vibhushan:** Second highest civilian award for exceptional and distinguished service.
• **Padma Bhushan:** Third highest civilian award for distinguished service of a high order.
• **Padma Shri:** Fourth highest civilian award for distinguished service in any field.
• Announced annually on **26th January** (Republic Day).
• **Mnemonic for Hierarchy:** **"Vibhuti Bhushan Shri"** -> **Vibhushan** (Top) -> **Bhushan** (Middle) -> **Shri** (Base).

items.title: 3. Sports Awards in India
items.content:
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:** Highest sporting honor, formerly known as **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna** (renamed in **2021**); carries a cash prize of **INR 25 Lakh**.
• **Arjuna Award:** Instituted in **1961** for consistent outstanding performance over 4 years; carries **INR 15 Lakh**.
• **Dronacharya Award:** Instituted in **1985** for excellence in sports coaching.
• **Dhyan Chand Award:** Instituted in **2002** for lifetime achievement in sports.
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy:** Given to the overall top-performing university in inter-university tournaments.

items.title: 4. International Literary & Academic Awards
items.content:
• **Nobel Prize:** Established by **Alfred Nobel** in **1901**; awarded in **6 fields** (Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economics).
• **Economic Sciences Nobel:** Added in **1969** (Sveriges Riksbank Prize).
• **Booker Prize:** Established in **1969** for best original novel written in English published in the UK/Ireland.
• **International Booker Prize:** Awarded for a translated fiction book into English.
• **Pulitzer Prize:** Established in **1917** by Joseph Pulitzer, administered by Columbia University for achievements in journalism, literature, and musical composition.

items.title: 5. Gallantry Awards in India
items.content:
• Divided into wartime and peacetime categories.
• **Wartime Gallantry Awards:** **Param Vir Chakra** (PVC - highest), **Maha Vir Chakra** (MVC), **Vir Chakra**.
• **Peacetime Gallantry Awards:** **Ashok Chakra** (highest peacetime), **Kirti Chakra**, **Shaurya Chakra**.
• Instituted on **26th January 1950** with retrospective effect from **15th August 1947**.
• **Mnemonic for Wartime Top 3:** **"PMV"** -> **P**aram Vir -> **M**aha Vir -> **V**ir.

items.definition: Use the acronym **"PEACE MED"** -> **P**hysics, **E**conomics, **A**rts (Literature), **C**hemistry, **E**conomics (Wait: Physics, Economics, Medicine, Chemistry, Literature, Peace). Better acronym: **"MEC LPP"** -> **M**edicine, **E**conomics, **C**hemistry, **L**iterature, **P**hysics, **P**eace.

Remember sequence: **"RTH MK AAY"** -> **R**abindranath Tagore (**1913**), **T**eresa (Mother, **1979**), **H**argobind Khorana (**1968**), **M**arshall (Venkatraman, **2009**), **K**ailash Satyarthi (**2014**), **A**martya Sen (**1998**), **A**bdus Salam (Pak-origin), **Y**es (Abhijit Banerjee, **2019**).
Recall **"R-C-R"** -> **R**ajagopalachari, **C**.V. Raman, **S**arvepalli Radhakrishnan (Radhakrishnan starts with R sound).
Size of name rule: **Padma Vibhushan** (longest name = highest), **Padma Bhushan** (medium name = middle), **Padma Shri** (shortest name = base).
Wartime top-to-bottom: **Param** (Supreme) -> **Maha** (Great) -> **Vir** (Brave). Peacetime top-to-bottom: **Ashok** (Emperor) -> **Kirti** (Fame) -> **Shaurya** (Valor).

items.term: Trick 6: Major Sports Award Cash Prizes
items.definition: Khel Ratna = **INR 25 Lakh**, Arjuna = **INR 15 Lakh**, Dronacharya (Lifetime) = **INR 15 Lakh**, Dronacharya (Regular) = **INR 10 Lakh**, Dhyan Chand = **INR 10 Lakh**.

items.term: Trick 7: Booker Prize vs International Booker
items.definition: **Booker** = English original (any nationality writing in English); **International Booker** = Translated into English from any language.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Arjuna Award Inception Year
items.definition: Students often confuse **1961** (Arjuna Award inception) with **1991** (Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna inception). Always remember Arjuna came much earlier.

items.term: Mistake 2: First Indian Nobel Winner vs First Indian Science Nobel Winner
items.definition: **Rabindranath Tagore** won the first Nobel for India (**1913**, Literature), whereas **C.V. Raman** won the first Science Nobel (**1930**, Physics).

items.term: Mistake 3: Bharat Ratna Max Limit per Year
items.definition: Many candidates think Bharat Ratna must be given every year. The correct rule is a **maximum of 3 recipients per year**, and it is not mandatory to award it annually.

items.term: Mistake 4: Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Renaming
items.definition: The award was officially renamed to **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **August 2021**, not 2020 or 2022.

Jnanpith is awarded for literature in languages included in the **8th Schedule of the Constitution plus English**, whereas Sahitya Akademi covers **24 languages** (22 scheduled + Rajasthani + English).

items.term: Mistake 6: Ashok Chakra vs Param Vir Chakra
items.definition: **Param Vir Chakra** is India's highest military decoration for wartime gallantry, while **Ashok Chakra** is the highest for peacetime gallantry.

upscNotes.content: Focus heavily on current affairs award winners from the past 1 year preceding the UPSSSC PET exam, especially Padma Awardees from Uttar Pradesh and national sports award winners.
Always memorize the first and latest Indian recipients of major international awards like the Nobel Prize, Booker Prize, and Oscar Awards.
UPSSSC frequently sets trap questions swapping the inception years of the Arjuna Award (1961) and Dronacharya Award (1985). Do not confuse them.
Questions often state that Bharat Ratna comes with a cash prize. Remember, it only comes with a medallion and a Sanad; there is **no monetary grant**.
Make a separate list of Uttar Pradesh personalities who received Padma Vibhushan or Padma Bhushan in the latest announcement for state-level exam relevance.

keyTakeaways: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in **1954** with a maximum limit of **3 recipients per year**.
Nobel Prizes are awarded annually on **10th December** across **6 categories**, with the Economics prize added in **1969**.
Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sports honor, carrying a cash prize of **INR 25 Lakh**.
Arjuna Award was established in **1961** and is given for consistent sporting performance over **4 years**.
Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honor, established in **1961**.
Wartime highest gallantry award is **Param Vir Chakra**, while peacetime highest is **Ashok Chakra**.
Dada Saheb Phalke Award is India's highest cinema recognition, instituted in **1969**.
